newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil poised to backwardate.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil poised to backwardate.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed at midday on Friday on signs of fresh buying from China and unexpected purchases by Thailand and are poised to move into backwardation within the next few days, traders said.
"Gas oil is picking up as there is some buying interest seen from China and supplies in Singapore are balanced," one trader said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.55/$25.65 per barrel up from Thursday's $25.15/$25.30, and traded earlier in the day at $25.59, brokers said.
April was last quoted at $25.40/$25.65 and brokers said the March/April spread is expected to trade at positive numbers very soon.

Traders said the tightening of prompt supplies in Singapore after recent exports to the Indian sub-continent totalling 80,000-tonnes and to Thailand (60,000-tonnes) are giving strength to the front month swaps.
Swaps quotes had risen despite lower overnight gas oil futures where March closed down $4.50 per tonne to $180.00 on the International Petroleum Exchange on Thursday.
The jet fuel market were steady after the recent collapse with the March regrade holding at $1.90/$2.30 per barrel.
Fuel oil swaps firmed in line with the physical market where the recent aggressive offers have all disappeared.
Sentiment has improved on the fuel oil market amid fresh demand from India and exports to Thailand.
March was last quoted at $101.50/$103.50 per tonne, from Thursday's $100.00/$101.00 per tonne.
